claims.text: A nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation can be incorporated into CoCrFeNi through in-situ TEM-guided processing.
The intervention will reduce the coefficient of friction by 30% relative to baseline CoCrFeNi.
The intervention will reduce wear rate by 40% relative to baseline CoCrFeNi.
The predicted friction reduction will be maintained from room temperature to 800 °C.
The predicted wear-rate reduction will be maintained from room temperature to 800 °C.
The nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation facilitates formation of an oxide layer.
The resulting oxide layer is self-lubricating.
The intervention enhances the alloy's ability to adapt to varying loads and environments.
Real-time observation and control of microstructural evolution produces the proposed adaptability.
The proposed performance applies at loads up to 1000 N.
The proposed performance applies under both humid and dry conditions.
The magnitude of friction and wear reduction may depend on processing conditions and the resulting microstructure.
Baseline CoCrFeNi without the nanohierarchical architecture is the experimental control.
Failure to reduce both coefficient of friction and wear rate by at least 20% at any point in the temperature range is designated as falsifying the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts 30% friction and 40% wear-rate reductions, but the falsification rule only requires 20% reductions. Results below the stated predictions could therefore avoid falsification.

The structural mediator identifies a self-lubricating oxide layer, whereas the mechanism attributes performance to real-time TEM observation and control. Observation is a processing or characterization activity rather than a material mechanism, and the fields do not explain how the oxide layer produces adaptability.
